t:
Schedule 8 is amended by striking out item 852.10 and the article description immediately preceding it, and by inserting after item 870.25 the following new item:




 
  “
  870.27
  Specimens of archeology, mineralogy, or natural history (including specimens of botany or zoology other than live zoological specimens) imported for any public or private scientific collection for erhibk tion or other educational or scientific use, and not for sale or other commercial use
  Free
  Free
  ”

fable.w: This section only amends a tariff schedule to give duty-free treatment to certain scientific specimens. The tempting reading is that the reference to a "public or private scientific collection" brings outside parties in, but that phrase merely describes the importers who qualify for the duty-free item. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given a right to challenge any federal decision, and no rulemaking, hearing, or advisory body is created.

Temptation: The text mentions "public or private scientific collection," which might suggest public involvement. However, this is merely a description of the type of goods being imported for tariff purposes, not a process for public participation in a government decision.

Resolution: This section amends a tariff schedule to grant duty-free status to certain imported specimens. It does not require consultation, hearings, or input from outside parties before the decision is made; it simply defines the scope of a tax exemption.
